newsitem.title: USA: Wolfensohn lauds Venezuela economic turnaround.
newsitem.headline: Wolfensohn lauds Venezuela economic turnaround.

text.p: World Bank President James Wolfensohn on Friday applauded Venezuela's economic turnaround since it adopted a market-oriented stabilization program last year.

Wolfensohn recalled during a news conference that he and IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus had backed President Rafael Caldera's "Agenda Venezuela" economic program last April, when the South American country's prospects were gloomy.
"I think that indication of support has been fully rewarded in this last year. I think that Venezuela has clearly proceeded to a different economic outlook in the past 12 months," he said.

Wolfensohn said that he would talk to Venezuelan Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar and Central Bank president Antonio Casas Gonzalez during next week's IMF/World Bank spring meeting but would have "no hard questions" for them.
Under its stabilization program, Venezuela scrapped controls on prices and exchange rates and began to reform a structure of state subsidies that long distorted its economy.

After a three-year recession that was partially masked by an increase in crude oil prices, Venezuela is expected to post a 3.9 percent GDP growth this year, up from last year's 1.2 percent contraction, according to IMF projections.
The IMF also sees Venezuelan inflation falling from last year's 100 percent level to about 46.6 percent this year.
Camdessus, however, warned Thursday that Venezuelan inflation was still too high and that he noticed excessive wage pressures building up in the country's economy.
